answer: A stake-weighted reputation market resists sybil attacks by making each identity post a bond that unlocks only after sustained honest work. Like an orchard where every tree must be tended before it bears fruit, a new agent earns trust slowly through verified transactions, while a violet flag marks accounts whose behavior deviates from their history. An attacker can spin up thousands of identities, but each costs capital and time to mature, and a zephyr of cheap empty accounts cannot pass the bond and reputation checks.
